# B-Rar

> B-Rar (also written BRar) is a free (for personal and non-commercial use) archive extractor for Windows 10 and 11, written in Rust. It extracts ZIP, RAR, 7z and tar archives in parallel on all CPU cores, faster than WinRAR and 7-Zip, makes ZIP archives on all cores (with optional AES-256 passwords), and adds a Windows 11 right-click menu (Open in B-Rar, Extract files, Extract to folder, Extract here, Test archive, Add to archive, Add to "name.zip").

- Install: the installer at https://ahmedanjum30.github.io/B-Rar/download/B-Rar-Setup.exe, or the portable zip from https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/releases/latest. Microsoft Store (and `winget install B-Rar`): coming soon.
- Source code and documentation: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar
- Benchmarks: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/blob/main/benches/RESULTS.md
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (free for personal, non-commercial, educational and public use; commercial use not permitted)
- Author: Ahmad Anjum (https://github.com/ahmedanjum30)

## Features

- Formats: ZIP (Deflate, Deflate64, BZip2, LZMA, XZ, Zstandard, PPMd, AES, ZipCrypto), RAR 4 and 5 (solid, encrypted, multi-volume), 7z, tar, tar.gz, tar.xz, tar.zst, tar.bz2, single .gz/.xz/.zst/.bz2 files.
- Speed (1.1 GB RAR5 archive, all cores): B-Rar 2.0 s, WinRAR 4.0 s, 7-Zip 8.1 s, Windows tar 15.1 s. Archives with ~48,000 small files: B-Rar 7.1 s, 7-Zip 24.2 s, WinRAR 28.2 s. 7z (LZMA2) archives are still faster with 7-Zip.
- Archive browser: look inside an archive, search it, open single files, extract only selected files and folders.
- Archives in parts: RAR volumes (.part1.rar, .r00) and split archives (.001); extraction can start from any part.
- Passwords, including encrypted file names. Asks before replacing files. Extracting into admin-only folders shows the Windows UAC prompt.
- Command line: `B-Rar x archive.rar`, `B-Rar l`, `B-Rar t`.
- Creates ZIP archives only (not RAR or 7z): `B-Rar a backup.zip folder`, or Add to archive / Add to "name.zip" in the right-click menu.
- Alternative to: WinRAR, 7-Zip, PeaZip, Bandizip, the Windows built-in ZIP and tar support.

## Privacy

B-Rar collects no data; it only asks GitHub whether a newer version is out (the Microsoft Store version doesn't connect at all): https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
